text: Team, investor, and advisor allocations are almost never liquid on day one. The near-universal pattern is a cliff — zero tokens unlock for an initial period — followed by linear vesting, where tokens unlock in equal increments, often monthly, until the full allocation is released.

Take a 4-year vesting schedule with a 1-year cliff on a 2,400,000 token allocation. At month 11, still inside the cliff, nothing has vested. At month 12, the cliff just ends — still zero. By month 24, 800,000 tokens have vested; by month 36, 1,600,000; by month 48, the full 2,400,000.

That's not a smooth ramp from day zero — nothing unlocks for the first 12 months, then the remaining 36 months release the allocation in equal monthly chunks of about 66,667 tokens. Plotted, it's a flat line at zero through the cliff, then a straight diagonal ramp to 100%.

Cliffs matter for four reasons. They align long-term incentives, since anyone who leaves before the cliff gets nothing. They prevent early dumping, since insiders can't sell immediately after launch into the demand it created. They signal confidence, since insiders accept illiquidity on the same terms they ask holders to accept risk.
And they protect price stability — spreading unlocks over years instead of releasing everything at once smooths out the sell-pressure spikes a single large unlock event would otherwise create.

Every vesting chart in a crypto investor deck is built from this same cliff-then-ramp shape, whether or not it's drawn explicitly. Next: designing sustainable incentives, and how all of these supply mechanics come together in one coherent system.
